create.name: Centro Buddhista Muni Gyana
create.bio:
Centro Buddhista Muni Gyana is Palermo's centre for Tibetan Mahayana Buddhism in the Gelug tradition, set on the slopes of Pizzo Sella above the city. Lama Zopa Rinpoche founded it in 1990 at the request of two local students, Rodolfo Bajardi and Elia Manto, and it belongs to the FPMT, the international network of monasteries and Dharma centres that looks to the Dalai Lama as its highest authority. A non-sectarian, non-profit association, it is also a member of the Italian Buddhist Union and has been building a group of stupas on its grounds.

Since 2020 its resident teacher has been the French monk Venerable Olivier Rossi, Lobsang Jamyang, who completed the Masters Program at the Lama Tzong Khapa Institute and leads the FPMT Basic Program here, a structured study of the whole Buddhist path in modules with meditation, discussion and exams. Weekly meditation meetings on the four foundations of mindfulness are open to beginners in person and online, and there are Tara practices, workshops such as mandala drawing, and visits from geshes and Tibetan lamas. Registered users can follow online courses, while members reach the full archive. The YouTube channel holds long recorded teachings on death and rebirth, karma, emptiness and Buddhism and science.

courses.title: Incontro di meditazione
courses.description: A regular evening meditation meeting, in person in Palermo and online, practising the four foundations of mindfulness (body, feelings, mind and phenomena); open to complete beginners. Led by Elvira Oliveri and Simona Trecarichi.

courses.title: Basic Program FPMT
courses.description: The FPMT's structured study of the whole Buddhist path, taught by Venerable Olivier Rossi in modules with study materials, meditations, discussion classes and an exam at the end of each module; enrol through the secretariat.

courses.title: Insegnamenti online – Corsi
courses.description: Recorded online courses on the centre's own platform, including an introduction to Buddhism and the nine stages of calm abiding; some are free after registration, and members can reach the full archive.
courses.price: Some free with registration; full access for members
